definition: Number of cycles a core executes per second. Higher clocks mean more instructions per unit time, but IPC (instructions per cycle) matters equally — a 4 GHz Zen 4 crushes a 4 GHz Pentium 4.
Guaranteed all-core frequency vs. maximum opportunistic single-core frequency under power/thermal headroom.
Physical execution units vs logical streams (SMT/Hyper-Threading). More threads help parallel workloads; games mostly want fast cores.
On-chip SRAM hierarchy. L3 shared among cores; AMD 3D V-Cache stacks extra L3 vertically for massive gaming gains.
Thermal Design Power — the cooling requirement watts, not necessarily peak electrical draw. Intel now publishes PL1/PL2 power limits separately.
Semiconductor feature size label (5 nm, 3 nm...). Smaller generally means more transistors per watt, but marketing names diverge from physical dimensions.
Physical/electrical CPU interface (AM5, LGA 1700). Determines motherboard compatibility and often memory generation.
Motherboard silicon providing I/O: PCIe lanes, USB, SATA, overclock permissions. Doesn’t affect raw CPU/GPU speed.
High-speed serial links. x16 for GPUs, x4 for NVMe. Version (3/4/5) doubles bandwidth per generation.
Simultaneous Multi-Threading (Intel calls it Hyper-Threading). Two instruction streams share one core’s resources, ~20–30% aggregate gain typically.
Instructions Per Cycle — architectural throughput. The main lever of generational CPU progress.
Wide vector instruction sets for scientific/AI workloads. Consumer chips vary: Zen 4 supports AVX-512 at reduced clocks; Raptor Lake disabled it.
Stored overclock profiles for RAM. XMP is Intel-origin, EXPO is AMD’s equivalent; enabling either runs memory beyond JEDEC defaults.
Clock cycles for a column read. Real latency = CL ÷ (MT/s ÷ 2000) in nanoseconds — why DDR5-6000 CL30 ≈ 10 ns.
Dual In-line Memory Module; U = unbuffered desktop; SO = small outline for laptops. Not interchangeable.
Error-correcting code RAM detects/corrects bit flips. Requires mobo+CPU support; essential for servers/workstations.
Graphics memory. Capacity governs texture/resolution headroom; type/bus/bandwidth govern how fast it feeds the GPU.
Parallel channel count between GPU and VRAM. Bandwidth = bus × memory clock.
Shader execution units. Comparable only within the same architecture family — cross-brand counts mislead.
Fixed-function accelerators for matrix math (DLSS/AI) and ray-box intersections (ray tracing).
Upscaling suites: NVIDIA deep-learning, AMD spatial+ML, Intel ML, PlayStation Spectral Super Resolution. Render lower, reconstruct sharper.
Inserting synthetic frames between real ones (DLSS3/FSR3). Doubles perceived smoothness; adds latency and needs solid base FPS.
Simulating light rays for reflections/shadows/GI. Costs huge compute; denoisers + upscalers make it practical.
Full-scene recursive ray simulation replacing raster entirely. Cyberpunk RT Ultra/Overdrive is the reference workload.
GPU power envelope; laptop variants (TGP) define actual performance of identically named mobile chips.
When textures exceed VRAM, spills to system RAM tank frametimes. Primary reason 8 GB cards age poorly.
Protocols for SSD transport. NVMe over PCIe unlocks SSD speed; AHCI is the SATA-era legacy path.
Terabytes Written endurance rating — warrantied total writes before cell wearout concerns.
Buffer chip smoothing writes; DRAM-less drives rely on slower HMB — visible in sustained large transfers.
Efficiency certification brackets (Bronze→Titanium) at 20/50/100% load. Says little about electrical quality — a known loophole.
Cables detach for cleaner builds: semi vs full modular. SFX/SFX-L form factors serve small cases.
Microsecond GPU power surges; ATX 3.0/3.1 spec mandates 2× TDP handling for two GPUs’ generations.
Shifting voltage-frequency curve downward for same clocks at less power/heat — the modern way to "overclock" efficiently.
AMD Precision Boost Overdrive — raises power/current/thermal limits so boost algorithms go harder.
Removing CPU IHS to replace TIM with direct-die cooling. Big temps drop, big risk; voids warranty.
When one component caps system performance. CPU-bound at low res/high FPS; GPU-bound at high res/settings.
Average FPS hides hitches; 1%-low frametimes define perceived smoothness. Always check both.
Our headline scores: GM of many normalized benchmarks — rewards balanced products, punishes narrow specialists.
Board/case size standards. ITX trades expandability for footprint; E-ATX exceeds standard towers.
Sealed pump+radiator liquid kit vs. user-assembled loop. Custom cools more hardware, demands maintenance.
High-pressure blade designs that push air through radiators/filters vs. open-flow volume fans.
Modern firmware interface replacing legacy BIOS: mouse input, networking, secure boot, larger boot disks.
Boot-chain signature enforcement + hardware root of trust. Required for certain OS installs and anti-cheat.
PCIe feature letting CPU access all GPU VRAM at once — free 3–8% in many titles when enabled.
SMT siblings share execution units; some security flaws (downfall-class) exploit shared state — patches can cost performance.
